To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the performance of the best performing methods in the literature is not satisfactory for predicting protein-protein interactions, and (ii) the performance of these methods can be significantly increased by combining them.

(1) the prediction capacity of individual verb pairs is not uniform, and (2) the prediction capacity is correlated with the number of interactions that have been annotated in the training data for each verb pair.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of protein-protein interactions from the literature.
the identification of protein-protein interactions from the sequence of proteins.
the identification and characterization of the functional interactions between proteins in the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, while the use of individual verbs in a sentence may be a good indication of a particular type of protein-protein interaction, this is only a weak indicator of a particular type
the prediction capacity of the individual verb is a function of both its semantic and its syntactic context.
the results obtained with our method are comparable to those of the state-of-the-art methods.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the prediction of interactions is not a problem of the method but a problem of the data.

it is possible to predict protein interactions based on a set of 10 verbs that describe protein interactions, but that it is not possible to predict the exact interaction partner of an individual protein.
we have shown that it is possible to identify protein interactions from a large number of individual verbs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the prediction capacity of individual words can be measured.
we should be more cautious about using individual verbs to infer interactions.
the capacity to predict interactions of a given protein is not uniform for different verbs.
